summary: Manchester United was founded in 1878 as Newton Heath L&YR Football Club.
The club entered the English First Division for the first time in the 1892-93 season.
The club moved to Old Trafford, its current stadium, in 1910.
The Old Trafford stadium was originally opened on February 19, 1910 with a capacity of approximately 80,000.
Manchester United Football Club was founded on 5 March 1878 as Newton Heath LYR Football Club and changed its name to Manchester United on 24 April 1902.
Manchester United won its first First Division (top-flight) league title in the 1907–08 season.
Manchester United became the first English club to win the European Cup in 1968, defeating Benfica 4–1 in the final.
The Los Angeles Dodgers moved to Los Angeles before the 1958 season and played their first four seasons at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.
Dodger Stadium, the current home of the Los Angeles Dodgers, is the third-oldest ballpark in Major League Baseball, after Fenway Park and Wrigley Field.

Since 2012, the Los Angeles Dodgers have been led by Guggenheim Baseball Management and a group of owners including Mark Walter, Magic Johnson, Todd Boehly, Bobby Patton Jr., Peter Guber, Billie Jean King, and Ilana Kloss.
The Los Angeles Dodgers have won seven World Series titles and 21 National League pennants.
